subject: Phased BYO-key rewrap, "revivification" windows & secret stewardship checkpoints
messages:
From: Samantha Wright <samantha.wright@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased BYO-key rewrap & secret stewardship checkpoints

Marissa / team —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and ops side as we scope the private deployment (VPC + on-prem HSM):

1) Rewrap cadence controls: we need a proposal for a phased "rewrap" (BYOK re-wrapping) that can be triggered either by time (monthly/quarterly), entropy threshold, or an anomalous telemetry spike (e.g., unusual outbound egress of wrapped tokens). Can you outline trigger semantics and minimum operator involvement?

2) Revivification window: we want a short, auditable timeframe during which a previous wrapping can be recovered for rollback before the new key fully replaces the old one. Typical ask is 24–72 hours. What do you recommend for safety vs. blast radius?

3) Proof-of-possession & audit evidence: our compliance team expects signed attestations when keys are rewrapped and a snapped snapshot of key-material logs. What artifacts can Redwood provide?

4) Secret stewardship: we need guidance on whether Redwood recommends an "operatorless" rewrap path (zero-human-operator) versus a deliberate operator checkpoint for high-sensitivity accounts.

I've attached our questionnaire (acme-byo-questionnaire.xlsx) which includes a sketch of our topology. Procurement is looped for cost questions (cc: procurement@acmehealth.com).

Can you reply with a short proposal and an initial cost delta estimate? If helpful, we can set a follow-up for next week.

Thanks,
Samantha Wright
Head of Infrastructure Security
Acme Health

Attachments: acme-byo-questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Wright <samantha.wright@acmehealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased BYO-key rewrap & secret stewardship checkpoints

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level response below; I'll attach a short proposal pdf with diagrams and a cost sketch by EOD Monday. Quick notes up front:

- Phased rewrap model: we propose a three-stage orchestration:
  * Stage 0 (Canary): rewrap a small set of tokens (10–25%) on a dedicated canary pool to validate unwrap/rewrap flows and telemetry.
  * Stage 1 (Bulk, conditional): proceed to bulk rewrap but gate by successful canary + no telemetry anomalies for a 2-hour observation window.
  * Stage 2 (Finalize): mark the new key as primary and initiate a 48-hour revivification window during which the old wrapping material is preserved and marked as deprecated.

- Triggers & semantics: rewrap can be scheduled (cron), triggered by entropy/health metrics (we already collect token unwrap rates, key usage histograms), or manually initiated. We recommend an "anomaly hold" that pauses progression if egress, unwrap-failure rate, or unexpected agent restarts exceed configured thresholds.

- Revivification window: default recommendation: 48 hours. Rationale: balances operational rollback vs. exposure. We can shorten to 24 hours for lower-risk workloads or extend to 72 for high-sensitivity accounts.

- Proof-of-possession & artifacts: Redwood will provide:
  * Signed event logs for every unwrap/rewrap transaction (SHA256 + timestamp + operator id or automation id).
  * Signed snapshot of the rewrap operation (manifest.json stub) and an optional notarized S3 object with checksums.
  * Audit bundle (pdf) containing timeline, operator steps, and telemetry summary for compliance ingest.

- Operatorless path: available as a mode. We call it "autonomous rewrap" — it requires stricter pre-conditions (entirely infra-level approvals, HSM policy permitting unattended rewrap, and a pre-registered emergency rollback token that lives off-network). For Acme Health's profile, recommend a hybrid: automated canary + manual gate for bulk, with ability to opt into fully automated rewrap for low-risk namespaces.

I'll attach a staged-rewrap-proposal.pdf with diagrams and operational checks; Soojin, can you weigh in on recommended thresholds and what audit package we should provide to meet Acme's SOC-like needs? Jasmine, I'll include a short runbook appendix you can share with Solutions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staged-rewrap-proposal.pdf (pdf)

Marissa / Samantha —

Quick procurement / ops clarifying Qs before we review the PDF:

- Cost delta: does the 3-stage orchestration materially increase token/unit pricing or is it an operational overlay with modest infra-hours? Can you provide a top-level delta table (canary bulk finalize) and an estimate for manual-operator-hours if we choose the hybrid path?

- Operator involvement: in the hybrid mode, what exact steps require human sign-off? We need to map to our on-call rotations, and determine if an on-call engineer in EMEA needs to be in the loop for certain calendar windows.

- Secret lifecycle: will Redwood hold any plaintext or unwrapped key material during the revivification window? We need a firm guarantee here.

Thanks — if you can reply with a short table, that will help us get procurement clearance.

Tom Ellis
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: samantha.wright@acmehealth.com, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 06 Jul 2028 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased BYO-key rewrap & secret stewardship checkpoints

Tom / Procurement team —

Short answers inline, plus the attached cost sheet and a link to the internal design doc.

- Cost delta: orchestration is primarily a control-plane capability. Expected delta: a nominal one-time integration/setup fee plus a small percent uplift (we've modeled 3–6% per-month under the hybrid rewrap schedule for large token volumes). See attached cost-impact-estimate.xlsx for line items (canary compute, additional audit retention, optional notarization fees).

- Operator steps (hybrid): human sign-off is required only at the gate between Stage 0 -> Stage 1 (canary success) unless you opt into fully autonomous mode. The sign-off is a simple approval in the Console (approve/reject) and can be granted by any member of a configured "rewrap-approvers" group (we can pre-register an on-call alias). If you want EMEA on-call included, we can add a time-windowed policy so rewrap gates require a regional approver during EMEA business hours.

- Secret lifecycle & plaintext: Redwood does NOT persist plaintext keys outside the HSM boundary. During the revivification window we keep the previous wrapping metadata and archived HSM event logs required to reconstruct the rewrap lineage, but no unwrapped key material ever leaves the HSM. We will include a signed attestation confirming that behavior in the audit bundle.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- We'll send the staged-rewrap-proposal.pdf + cost sheet to procurement and schedule a 30-min sync to walk through thresholds.
- Soojin will propose threshold defaults (unwrap-failure > 0.5% in 5 mins, egress exceedance > 1.2x baseline, etc.).
- Jasmine will add a minimal runbook for your on-call rotations and a template approval message for the Console gate.

Thanks — happy to join a call if Procurement prefers a quick walkthrough.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
